activities.desc: Depart from Pittsburgh (PIT) or Morgantown (MGW). EDT → CEST (+6h)
Stroll the harbor promenade with shops, restaurants, and marina views
Munch's The Scream, Viking gold, and Norwegian art. Indoor, central, jet-lag-friendly
Walk the sloping marble roof for iconic city + fjord views
200+ bronze, granite, and iron sculptures in Frogner Park. The Angry Boy and Monolith are crowd-pleasers
Mathallen Oslo food hall with diverse dinner options

groupNotes: Arrive in Oslo. Keep Day 1 light - outdoor walking only, no indoor museums longer than 1 hour. Vigeland Park: open air, easy walking. The Opera House roof is a must for sunset. Early dinner in Grünerløkka.

lodging.name: Citybox Oslo
lodging.pros: Self-check-in 24/7, central near Oslo Central Station, modern minimalist rooms, free Wi-Fi
lodging.cons: No breakfast, no daily housekeeping, small rooms

lodging.name: Radisson RED Oslo
lodging.pros: Modern Scandinavian design, excellent breakfast bar, great location near Opera House and waterfront
lodging.cons: Standard chain feel, no pool, can be noisy

lodging.name: Grand Hotel Oslo
lodging.pros: Historic 1874 property, Nobel Peace Prize venue, rooftop terrace, exceptional breakfast, prime Karl Johans gate location
lodging.cons: Very expensive, some rooms dated, tourist crowds

meals.lunch: Godt Brød coffee shop (skolebrød) or Mathallen Oslo food hall
meals.dinner: Mathallen Oslo food hall - each person picks their own vendor. Vulkanfisk for seafood soup, Bjørns for fårikål, or Høst for Norwegian small plates. Afterwards, walk along the Akerselva river or grab a drink at Hallen Cocktailbar

activities.desc: Play an early morning round at Krokhol, consistently ranked as one of the absolute top 2 disc golf courses in the entire world, located just 20 minutes southeast of downtown Oslo.
Polar exploration ship on Bygdøy. Walk inside the actual Fram. Interactive exhibits throughout
Modern art + forest trails with panoramic Oslo Fjord views. Light hike on wooded paths
Oslo's main street. Shops, cafés, people-watching
Medieval castle and fortress overlooking Oslo Fjord. Cannons and ramparts on display

groupNotes: Full day to explore Oslo. Early Morning: Play a memorable round at Krokhol Disc Golf Course (#1-2 ranked globally). Afternoon: Fram Museum or shop Karl Johans gate. Evening: Akershus Fortress for sunset views.

lodging.name: Citybox Oslo

lodging.cons: No breakfast, no daily housekeeping, small rooms

lodging.cons: Standard chain feel, no pool, can be noisy

lodging.name: Grand Hotel Oslo

lodging.cons: Very expensive, some rooms dated, tourist crowds

meals.lunch: Fram Museum café - waffles and brown cheese with fjord views
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schrøder - historic 1910 Norwegian tavern. Kjøttkaker (meatballs with lingonberry jam), fårikål (lamb and cabbage stew - Norway's national dish), and rice cream for dessert. After dinner, walk through the palace gardens or enjoy a nightcap at the Grand Hotel rooftop bar

directions: Exit onto E134 at Drammen towards Notodden
Continue on E134 through the Telemark valley to Rjukan
Brief detour to Heddal Stave Church near Notodden

stops.name: Kongsberg Silver Mines
stops.desc: Historic silver mines with underground train tour

stops.name: Heddal Stave Church
stops.desc: Norway's LARGEST stave church, built c.1250. Triple nave design. The most impressive stave church on the route

activities.desc: Norway's largest stave church. Triple nave, built 1250. More impressive than Borgund for sheer size
Scenic route through Telemark - deep valleys, historic farms, dramatic mountain passes
UNESCO World Heritage town. Giant mirrors on the mountain reflect winter sunlight into the valley - the sun mirror story is incredible

groupNotes: Easy drive day. Heddal Stave Church is a must-stop - biggest in Norway and genuinely impressive. Arrive Rjukan mid-afternoon. Explore the town - the sun mirror story and heavy water history set up Day 4.

lodging.name: Rjukan Hytteby
lodging.pros: Private cabins with kitchen facilities, affordable for groups, scenic location near lake, free parking
lodging.cons: No restaurant, self-catering only, 10-min drive from Rjukan center, basic cabins

lodging.name: Rjukan Hotell
lodging.pros: Historic town hotel with original 1900s charm, central Rjukan location, good breakfast, walking distance to Vemork museum
lodging.cons: Older building with some dated rooms, limited restaurant hours, no pool

lodging.name: Gausta View
lodging.pros: Mountain lodge at Gaustatoppen base, stunning summit views, modern cabins with full kitchen, ski-in/ski-out in winter, sauna access
lodging.cons: 15-min drive from Rjukan town, must self-cater, no restaurant on site

meals.lunch: Road picnic - Kiwi supermarket in Notodden: fresh bread, Norvegia cheese, Kvikk Lunsj
meals.dinner: Vessia Kro - classic Norwegian roadhouse in the mountains. Reindeer burger with brunost sauce, or slow-cooked moose stew. After dinner, soak in the mountain views from the hotel lounge

activities.desc: WWII Norwegian heavy water sabotage - the Heroes of Telemark! A gripping story of wartime sabotage
Hike Norway's most iconic peak (1,883m) or take the unique tram INSIDE the mountain. Both routes lead to the same epic summit view (1/6 of Norway!)
Northern Europe's oldest cable car (1928) is closed for renovation until 2028. Alternative: Rjukan Brewery offers a cozy visit with local culture and valley views
Local craft brewery in a historic building. Adults sample; teens get sodas

groupNotes: One of the most unique days in Norway. Morning: Vemork Museum - the heavy water sabotage story is riveting (read about it beforehand). Mid-day: Gaustabanen tram ride through the mountain - unforgettable. Late afternoon: Rjukan Brewery for a relaxed tasting.

lodging.name: Rjukan Hytteby
lodging.pros: Private cabins with kitchen facilities, affordable for groups, scenic location near lake, free parking
lodging.cons: No restaurant, self-catering only, 10-min drive from Rjukan center, basic cabins

lodging.name: Rjukan Hotell
lodging.pros: Historic town hotel with original 1900s charm, central Rjukan location, good breakfast, walking distance to Vemork museum
lodging.cons: Older building with some dated rooms, limited restaurant hours, no pool

lodging.name: Gausta View
lodging.pros: Mountain lodge at Gaustatoppen base, stunning summit views, modern cabins with full kitchen, ski-in/ski-out in winter, sauna access
lodging.cons: 15-min drive from Rjukan town, must self-cater, no restaurant on site

meals.lunch: Vemork Museum café - soup and sandwiches in a historic power station
meals.dinner: Gaustablikk Høyfjellshotell restaurant - mountain lodge dining with panoramic views. Reindeer fillet with lingonberry sauce, mountain trout, or traditional sodd (mutton soup with meatballs). After dinner, relax by the fireplace

directions: Take RV37 north from Rjukan onto Hardangervidda plateau
Cross Hardangervidda - Europe's largest mountain plateau at 1,200m+
Stop at Hardangervidda National Park visitor center
Arrive at Eidfjord on the Hardangerfjord

stops.name: Hardangervidda Plateau viewpoint
stops.desc: Norway's largest national park. Wild reindeer herds, vast plateau at 1,250m

stops.name: Vøringsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Norway's most famous waterfall - 182m free-fall. New cliff-side viewing platforms built into the rock

stops.name: Hardanger Cider Farm (Ulvik)
stops.desc: Hardanger cider farm tour with apple and pear cider tasting

activities.desc: Drive across Europe's largest mountain plateau. Reindeer sightings likely. The vast, otherworldly landscape is unforgettable
182m waterfall. New platforms cut into the cliff. Peer over the edge (safely!)
Peaceful village right on the Hardangerfjord. Boats, mountains, sunset over the water

groupNotes: The Hardangervidda crossing is magical - a completely different world at 1,200m. Travel in convoy since the plateau road is remote. Stop at the national park center. Vøringsfossen is jaw-dropping - the new platforms let you look straight down 182m. Arrive Eidfjord late afternoon.

lodging.name: Eidfjord Gjestehus
lodging.pros: Historic inn, Norwegian charm, affordable, central Eidfjord, shared kitchen, good budget base
lodging.cons: Shared bathrooms in some rooms, older building, limited restaurant hours

lodging.name: Eidfjord Fjell & Fjord Hotel
lodging.pros: Modern mountain-style hotel, panoramic Hardangerfjord views, restaurant with local ingredients, free parking
lodging.cons: Limited dining options nearby, quiet area, no pool

lodging.name: Quality Hotel Vøringfoss
lodging.pros: Floor-to-ceiling waterfall views of Vøringsfossen from many rooms, modern architecture, full-service restaurant with local Hardanger specialties, spa facilities
lodging.cons: Pricey, remote location requires car, waterfall noise may disturb light sleepers

meals.lunch: Hardangervidda National Park Center café - hot soup and fresh bread. Best reindeer soup on the plateau
meals.dinner: Vik Café & Restaurant - on the Eidfjord harbor. Fresh grilled salmon with Hardanger apples, or local lamb shank. Pair with Hardanger cider (traditional fruit wine from local orchards). After dinner, walk the Eidfjord waterfront at golden hour

activities.desc: Easy-to-moderate hike to a stunning blue lake below a glacier arm of Folgefonna. Observe safely from designated view lines; entering active ice hazard zones without certified guides is strictly prohibited.

activities.text: Hardanger fruit farm tour & cider tasting
activities.desc: Visit a local fruit farm. Taste apples, pears, Hardanger apple cider, and fresh-pressed juice
Guided sea kayak through the fruit orchard-lined fjord. Stillwater, suitable for all skill levels
Drive through the fruit orchard region. Snow-capped peaks above, apple blossoms below (late May/early June!)

groupNotes: Full day in Hardangerfjord - one of Norway's most beautiful regions. Morning: Bondhusbreen glacier valley trail. Afternoon: visit a fruit farm for cider tasting or kayak the fjord. The fruit farms are especially lovely in late May/early June with apple blossoms in bloom.

lodging.name: Eidfjord Gjestehus
lodging.pros: Historic inn, Norwegian charm, affordable, central Eidfjord, shared kitchen, good budget base
lodging.cons: Shared bathrooms in some rooms, older building, limited restaurant hours

lodging.name: Eidfjord Fjell & Fjord Hotel
lodging.pros: Modern mountain-style hotel, panoramic Hardangerfjord views, restaurant with local ingredients, free parking
lodging.cons: Limited dining options nearby, quiet area, no pool

lodging.name: Quality Hotel Vøringfoss
lodging.pros: Floor-to-ceiling waterfall views of Vøringsfossen from many rooms, modern architecture, full-service restaurant with local Hardanger specialties, spa facilities
lodging.cons: Pricey, remote location requires car, waterfall noise may disturb light sleepers

meals.lunch: Fruit farm café - Hardanger apple cake with a view over the fjord
meals.dinner: Eidfjord Gjestehus restaurant - traditional Norwegian lamb shank with Hardanger apple compote, or fresh trout from the fjord. Local cider is a must. After dinner, relax at the hotel with a board game in the common lounge

directions: Cross the Hardanger Bridge heading north
Follow RV13 north to Voss for family white-water rafting
Take the E16 west corridor from Voss directly to Bergen
Fantoft Disc Golf near Bergen city center

stops.name: Voss Rafting Center
stops.desc: Class 2-3 rapids on Raundalselva River. Guide, wetsuit, gear included. Minimum age 8

stops.name: Steinsdalsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Famous walk-behind waterfall located near Norheimsund. Accessible via optional scenic western loop bypass.

activities.desc: Cross one of the longest suspension bridges in the world spanning the inner fjord.
Mild class 2-3 rapids on the Raundalselva. Guide and gear included
Wooded course near Fantoft Stave Church. 10 min from Bergen city center
Arrive Bergen by late afternoon. Walk through the Hanseatic wharf's colorful wooden buildings

groupNotes: Efficient routing north from Eidfjord over the bridge directly up to Voss for the rafting window. Take the main fast E16 link west to Bergen for a clean afternoon flow. Hit Fantoft Disc Golf before checking into the hotel.

lodging.name: Citybox Bergen
lodging.pros: Self-check-in 24/7, near Bergen Station, clean modern rooms, free Wi-Fi, great value
lodging.cons: No breakfast, small rooms, no daily housekeeping

lodging.name: Zander K Hotel
lodging.pros: Design boutique hotel, excellent breakfast, central Bergen near train station, cool lobby with bar
lodging.cons: Some rooms small, no pool

lodging.name: Hotel Norge by Scandic
lodging.pros: Historic Bergen landmark, rooftop pool with city views, full spa, multiple restaurants, prime location near city park
lodging.cons: Very expensive, large hotel, some rooms feel corporate

meals.lunch: Voss Rafting Center cafe - burgers and coffee for the family
meals.dinner: Bare Vestland - modern twist on traditional Norwegian. Pickled herring, reindeer tartare, cloudberry dessert, and the best aquavit list in town. After dinner, walk through the Bryggen wharf lit up at night for photos

activities.desc: Cable car 320m up for panoramic Bergen views. Walking trails and playground at top. Steep ride with city views
World-famous indoor/outdoor market. Fresh seafood, local specialties. Grab a shrimp sandwich
UNESCO wharf and museum about German Hanseatic merchants
Bergen's highest mountain (643m). Restaurant at top with 360° views. Even better than Fløyen

groupNotes: Full day in Bergen. Morning: Fløibanen - the funicular is a Bergen institution. Fish Market for lunch. Afternoon: explore the Bryggen museum, browse the Fish Market, or visit the Hanseatic Museum. Late afternoon: Ulriken cable car. Evening: sunset drinks atop Mt. Fløyen.

lodging.name: Citybox Bergen
lodging.pros: Self-check-in 24/7, near Bergen Station, clean modern rooms, free Wi-Fi, great value
lodging.cons: No breakfast, small rooms, no daily housekeeping

lodging.pros: Design boutique hotel, excellent breakfast, central Bergen near train station, cool lobby with bar
lodging.cons: Some rooms small, no pool

lodging.pros: Historic Bergen landmark, rooftop pool with city views, full spa, multiple restaurants, prime location near city park
lodging.cons: Very expensive, large hotel, some rooms feel corporate

meals.lunch: Fish Market - fresh shrimp sandwich, fish soup, or a whale sausage for the adventurous
meals.dinner: Pingvinen - Bergen's best traditional pub. Raspeballer (potato dumplings - a Norwegian West Coast classic) with lamb and gravy, local Hansa beer on tap. After dinner, explore the bars on Nygårdsgaten or relax at the hotel

activities.desc: Sightseeing cruise through narrow straits. The boat squeezes through cliffs so narrow you can almost touch both sides
Guided kayak through Bergen's harbor. Paddle past Bryggen from the water
Bryggen artisan shops and Galleriet center. Norwegian wool sweaters, troll figurines, brunost
Final dinner. Bryggen Tracteursted (historic, traditional) or Lysverket (modern Nordic, Michelin-listed)

groupNotes: Last full day in Norway! Morning: Mostraumen fjord cruise - the boat gets SO close to the cliffs. Afternoon: kayak or explore more of Bergen. Evening: farewell dinner at Bryggen Tracteursted - one of Norway's oldest restaurants, right in the Hanseatic wharf.

meals.lunch: Godt Brød Bergen - skolebrød (custard-filled cardamom buns) and open-faced sandwiches
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Bryggen Tracteursted - candlelit dining in a 1708 Hanseatic merchant building. Reindeer stew, fresh salmon, and a final aquavit toast. Perfect finale to the trip

activities.desc: CEST → EDT (-6h). Connect via major European hubs. Return to regional destination terminal.
Last walk through Bryggen. One more kanelbolle at Godt Brød. Or tour Fantoft Stave Church (reconstructed, 15 min from city)
Norwegian wool, brunost, peppermakkels, aquavit

groupNotes: Departure day from Bergen (BGO). Good connections to European hubs. If on similar flights, arrange a shared transfer.

meals.lunch: Bergen Airport - last salmon grab or sandwiches for the plane
